chapter.title: Inter-partition communication
chapter.para: Partitions communicate only through ports. A port is an end of a channel that the configuration draws between ports of partitions; it is either a sampling port, which holds the latest message, or a queuing port, which holds a queue of messages. Every port has a direction, source (out) or destination (in).

section.para: JetOS shall let a partition communicate with other partitions only through the ports that the configuration gives it.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Channels are the only way for partitions to exchange data, so that the flow of information is as configured.

section.para: JetOS shall deliver the messages that a partition writes to a source port to the destination port at the other end of its channel, whole and unchanged.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A message must arrive as it was sent.

section.para: JetOS shall create a port at the request of its partition only while the partition is not in NORMAL mode, and only if the name is that of a port of the partition in the configuration and the maximum message size, the direction and, for a queuing port, the maximum number of messages of the request agree with it.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A port is what the configuration says, and the set of ports is fixed once the partition runs.

section.para: JetOS shall refuse with an error a request of a partition to create a port in NORMAL mode, with a name that is not that of a port of the partition in the configuration, or with a maximum message size, direction or maximum number of messages that does not agree with the configuration.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The partition must know that it has no port to use.

section.para: JetOS shall give a partition the identifier of a created port, found by its name, and the status of a port: for a sampling port its maximum message size, direction, refresh period and the validity of the last message that was read, for a queuing port its maximum message size, direction, maximum and present number of messages, and the number of processes waiting.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The partition has to find and to inspect its ports.

section.para: JetOS shall make the ports of a partition unusable when the partition restarts, so that the partition has to create them again.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Each start of a partition begins with no ports.

section.para: JetOS shall not let a partition use a port of another partition.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Ports are identified in the partition that created them only.

section.para: JetOS shall keep in a sampling channel only the latest message.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A sampling port is for data that is refreshed, where only the newest value counts.

section.para: JetOS shall store a message of a sampling source port by replacing the message that was there, with the time of writing.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A sampling port is for data that is refreshed, where only the newest value counts.

section.para: JetOS shall give the process that reads a sampling destination port the latest message with its length, without removing it, and whether it is valid, that is not older than the refresh period of the port.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A reader must know whether the data is fresh enough to use.

section.para: JetOS shall refuse at its creation a sampling port whose refresh period is not finite and positive.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Without a refresh period the validity of a message cannot be decided.

section.para: JetOS shall tell, on request, whether a sampling destination port has a message that has not been read yet.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A reader can see if there is anything new before it reads.

section.para: JetOS shall keep the messages of a queuing channel in the order in which they were sent, deliver each one at most once, and give the receiver the message that was sent first.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A queuing port is for data that must not be lost or reordered.

section.para: JetOS shall let a process send a message to a queuing source port at once if the queue has room and no process is waiting to send before it.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the blocking semantics of the queuing ports of ARINC 653.

section.para: JetOS shall make a process that sends a message to a queuing source port whose queue has no room, or on which another process is waiting to send, wait up to its time-out (none, for no waiting; or infinite) until there is room, and report an error for a time-out.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the blocking semantics of the queuing ports of ARINC 653.

section.para: JetOS shall let a process receive a message from a queuing destination port at once if there is one and no process is waiting to receive before it.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the blocking semantics of the queuing ports of ARINC 653.

section.para: JetOS shall make a process that receives from a queuing destination port that has no message, or on which another process is waiting to receive, wait up to its time-out until a message arrives, and report an error for a time-out.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the blocking semantics of the queuing ports of ARINC 653.

section.para: JetOS shall wake the processes that wait on a queuing port in the order in which they began to wait or in the order of their priorities, as the discipline of the port that the partition set when creating it says.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The discipline is a choice of the application.

section.para: JetOS shall wake a process that waits on a port when the partition of the other end of the channel has made it possible, although that partition runs only in its own slots.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Partitions run in different slots but their ports are linked.

section.para: JetOS shall, if a message of a queuing channel cannot be queued because the receiving side is full, discard the new message when the channel is set to do so.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A receiver that is slower than the sender must know that it lost data.

section.para: JetOS shall tell the receiver of a queuing channel that discarded messages, when it next receives, that messages have been lost.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A receiver that is slower than the sender must know that it lost data.

section.para: JetOS shall discard the messages that are in the queue of a queuing destination port when the partition clears it.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A partition can drop what it does not want any more.
